title: What Newborn Parenting Is and Why It Matters
summary: The foundations of newborn parenting: what it is and why getting it right pays off.
body:
Newborns (0-3 months): feed every 2-3 hours, sleep 14-17 hours in fragments, and need skin-to-skin, safe sleep (back, bare crib), and parents who accept help.

Why it matters: Feed every 2-3 hours (breast or formula) Safe sleep: back to sleep, bare crib, room-share 6-12 months

This guide walks the full ladder — foundations first, then compounded practice, then advanced mastery. Every record is actionable: read in order, do the steps, run the numbers.

title: Getting Started: Your First Five Moves in Newborn Parenting
summary: Start newborn parenting this week with five concrete moves.
body:
Don't try to do everything. Do these five, in order:

1. Feed on demand, every 2-3 hours
2. Burp mid- and post-feed
3. Safe sleep every time
4. Track feeds/diapers the first weeks
5. Accept all offered help

Five moves, one week. Momentum beats perfection — the rest of this guide builds on exactly this start.

title: Essential Tools and Supplies for Newborn Parenting
summary: What you actually need for newborn parenting — no more, no less.

The toolkit:

Buy the basics first. Upgrade only when a limit — not a whim — demands it.

title: Common Newborn Parenting Mistakes and How to Avoid Them
summary: The mistakes everyone makes with newborn parenting — and the fixes.
body:
The classic errors:

- No help accepted (burnout) → Fix: address it in your first week, not after it costs you.
- Unsafe sleep setups → Fix: address it in your first week, not after it costs you.
- Comparing to other babies → Fix: address it in your first week, not after it costs you.
- Skipping your own meals/rest → Fix: address it in your first week, not after it costs you.

Every mistake above is cheap to prevent and expensive to repair. Prevention is the whole game.

title: Newborn Parenting Beginner FAQ
summary: Straight answers to the most common newborn parenting questions.
body:
Q: How often to feed?
A: Every 2-3 hours; wake to feed early on.

Q: When to call the doctor?
A: Fever 100.4F+, poor feeding, few wet diapers.

Q: Sleep through the night?
A: Not yet - 3-4 hour stretches are the win.

Still stuck? Start with record 2 of this guide and do the first move today.

title: Newborn Parenting: Safety, Legal, and Fine Print
summary: What to watch out for with newborn parenting: safety, contracts, and fine print.
body:
Read before you act: No help accepted (burnout) And: Unsafe sleep setups

General rules: get agreements in writing, understand what you're signing, keep records of money in and out, and know when a professional (lawyer, accountant, vet, doctor — depending on the domain) is worth the fee. An hour of professional advice beats a month of fixing.

title: Doing Newborn Parenting With Others: Family and Team Edition
